evidence: Read _CATALOG_VIEWS at rule_sets.py:103-141. TABLES lists 21 fields (TABLE_CATALOG..TABLE_COMMENT), COLUMNS lists 22 fields (TABLE_CATALOG..GENERATION_EXPRESSION, SRS_ID), KEY_COLUMN_USAGE lists 12 fields (CONSTRAINT_CATALOG..REFERENCED_COLUMN_NAME). Each matches the MySQL 8.0 reference-manual column list for that view, in order. SRS_ID is present in COLUMNS, as it is since 8.0.3. Caveat: the comparison is against the documented MySQL 8.0 definitions, from my own knowledge of them. No MySQL server or doc source was available to run against, and I did not run the connector test. Releases 8.0.0-8.0.2 predate SRS_ID, which is a negligible edge. Absolute-claim trace: a field missing from the tuples would drop out of SELECT *, and each tuple was compared field by field with no omission or reordering.

Installed sqlglot 30.31.0 (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sqlglot-30.31.0.dist-info). generators/mysql.py:842-843 currentschema_sql returns self.func('SCHEMA'), so exp.CurrentSchema() renders SCHEMA() under mysql. parsers/mysql.py:151-152 maps both 'SCHEMA' and 'DATABASE' to exp.CurrentSchema.from_arg_list, so DATABASE() parses to the same node. rule_sets.py:327 builds exp.CurrentSchema() in _in_schema. Round-trip text comparison therefore matches.

rule_sets.py:321-323 _binary builds exp.Cast(this=node, to=DataType.build('BINARY', dialect='mysql')). sqlglot (.venv site-packages, generators/mysql.py:709-717) cast_sql only rewrites types in CAST_MAPPING (lines 321-337: TEXT/BLOB/VARCHAR->CHAR, ints->SIGNED, UBIGINT->UNSIGNED); BINARY is absent, and TYPE_MAPPING (260-278) has no BINARY entry, so base generator.py datatype_sql:1844 emits type_value.value 'BINARY' and cast_sql (generator.py:4360-4369) gives 'CAST(x AS BINARY)'. Parsing: the standard CAST parse reads AS BINARY via _parse_types into a DataType BINARY (mysql parsers/mysql.py:714-718 also treats the BINARY prefix as Cast to a DataType), which regenerates the same text. _is_catalog_derived (rule_sets.py:439-465) compares _generate(body) text with the _generate(_catalog_body(...)) text, so the reparsed body generates identically and is accepted. This was established by reading source; I did not run the roundtrip.

The claim depends on MySQL optimizer behavior (derived-table merge and condition pushdown with LIMIT). The repository only emits the SQL: src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:143-146 defines _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = "18446744073709551615" with a comment making the same claim, and tests/unit/test_safety_rule_sets.py:320-325,374,386 assert the LIMIT is appended to the derived tables. No MySQL source was provided (no dependency_sources) and no MySQL server run was possible. The known documented rule (a derived table containing LIMIT is not mergeable and conditions are not pushed into it) supports the claim, and the outer expressions in the select list, JOIN ON or ORDER BY would run over the materialized, already-filtered rows. However, I could not confirm that the optimizer treats the value 18446744073709551615 (equal to HA_POS_ERROR, the 'no limit' sentinel) as a real LIMIT clause on every supported MySQL version. Not verified: running EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE on SELECT ... FROM (SELECT ... LIMIT 18446744073709551615) AS t JOIN ... ON <error-raising expr> against MySQL 8.0 and 8.4.

rule_sets.py:146 defines _MATERIALIZE_LIMIT = "18446744073709551615" (2^64-1), used at :390 via exp.Literal.number(...). 2^64-1 is the documented maximum of MySQL LIMIT (unsigned BIGINT; the MySQL manual's 'retrieve all rows to end of table' example uses exactly this value). sqlglot's Literal.number builds a non-string Literal from the given text and emits it verbatim, so it is accepted as a numeric literal. Based on reading the source plus established knowledge of MySQL docs; sqlglot library source was not read from dependency_sources.

rule_sets.py:227-238 _catalog_view returns None unless table.this is an Identifier, db arg is an Identifier, catalog arg is None, and db.name.lower() == _INFORMATION_SCHEMA; then view = table.name.upper() must be in _CATALOG_VIEWS. Callers (_analyze :267-274) send a None result to _check_reference (:211-224), which refuses any catalog/db qualifier (KIND_CATALOG or KIND_QUALIFIED_TABLE, e.g. def.information_schema.tables has a catalog arg so _catalog_view returns None and it is refused), refuses non-Identifier sources, and refuses unlisted names. Backtick-quoted `information_schema` is still an exp.Identifier, so it is accepted as a catalog view, consistent with the claim (Identifier, case-insensitive). Absolute-input trace: def.information_schema.tables -> catalog set -> None -> refused at :215-219.

rule_sets.py:340-370 _catalog_filter, non-TABLES/COLUMNS branch (KEY_COLUMN_USAGE): own = connected-schema check on TABLE_SCHEMA AND (TABLE_NAME, COLUMN_NAME) IN listed pairs; no_reference = REFERENCED_TABLE_SCHEMA/NAME/COLUMN_NAME all IS NULL; listed_reference = REFERENCED_TABLE_SCHEMA = CURRENT_SCHEMA() AND (REFERENCED_TABLE_NAME, REFERENCED_COLUMN_NAME) IN the same pairs; result = own AND (no_reference OR listed_reference), parenthesized. Rows referencing another database, unlisted tables or unlisted columns fail both disjuncts and are hidden; partially NULL references are also hidden. Matches the claim. Absolute-claim input traced: FK row referencing another schema fails the schema equality, so it is hidden.

rule_sets.py:321-337,346-353 wrap only the catalog column side in CAST(... AS BINARY) (_binary); the literals (exp.Literal.string at 334, 351) are plain strings. In MySQL a binary string vs nonbinary string comparison is bytewise, so collation differences (utf8mb3 columns vs connection collation) are irrelevant: this part holds. The existence check in safety/relations.py:173-174 uses the same BINARY x = BINARY y pattern. However the claim says 'regardless of ... charset': the literal's bytes are in the connection charset, and the repo never sets it (grep for charset/character_set in src found nothing; it comes from the driver/URL). For non-ASCII identifiers under a non-utf8 connection charset (e.g. latin1) the literal bytes would differ from the utf8mb3 column bytes, so the charset-independence part cannot be settled by reading; it needs a MySQL run (not performed). Collation independence is established, charset independence is not.

Trigger-condition split. Code condition read: the OR in listed/no_reference, the AND in own, and _catalog_view/_analyze routing. Alternatives:
- no_reference branch -> outside the trigger: it only passes rows with all referenced fields NULL, which are PK or unique rows already limited by `own` to listed pairs and the current schema, so no input inside the trigger breaks it.
- listed_reference branch -> outside the trigger: it is the required FK row, and it checks schema and listed pairs.
- Non-matching catalog-name shapes (catalog-qualified, other schema) -> outside the trigger: _check_reference refuses them (KIND_CATALOG), and they are not reads of KEY_COLUMN_USAGE under the set.
- DATABASE() NULL -> outside the trigger: NULL equality gives no rows, which fails closed.
